items.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: Did you ever play with him? No, no. Never ever.

ctx.x: If you want to learn a song it used to be you’d put the record on and you’d play, you’d listen for those bass note. And now you can type it up and there it is for you. And you can start to depend on it.

Yeah well that’s the problem, because I’ve had people that I’ve taught and then I’ve run into them years later. They go on the gig with a little fake book sitting right there. That just turns me off. Maybe it’s okay. But back in the day which as far as I’m concerned from 1945 to 1965, that was when jazz was at its peak. And most of those groups then, if they weren’t big bands, parts of them, Cannonball Adderley, Miles Davis, you never saw © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

them with music on the bandstand. Think about it. They would be dressed up, and they didn’t do it. So that’s what happened to me. So I came up in that period. And that was all in line with having the ears and everything. And I ran into a shop when I got to the place where I was going to play on Broadway. Because for ten years I hadn’t read any music, although I had gone to a conservatory and studied sight reading and all that stuff. I had formal ear training before I got with Mary Lou, in school.…
